sampling_model.design: One target and \(J\) fixed donors are observed for \(n\) pre-treatment dates partitioned into \(L\) known proportional blocks; only the \(J\) untreated donors enter the \(T_1\) stable post-regime sample used for risk estimation.
sampling_model.units: The cross section is fixed. Pre-block and post-regime means obey the rank-\(r\) factor representation; \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\) then implies \(a_0\in\operatorname{col}(A)\) and \(d\in\operatorname{row}(A)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target may be treated in the post period, but its post outcomes are excluded from the observed-data experiment for \(R_P\).
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed; identification is the row-span completion induced by the stable common-loading model.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate block means and donor post means by averages, \(\Sigma\) by pre-block-demeaned residual second moments, and their joint long-run covariance by block/HAC scores. The local optimality theorem uses the exact information in Gaussian block means and pre/post scatter statistics.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish sparse predictor selection consistency and a faster predictor-match mean-squared-error rate, without inference for population prediction risk along the tuning path.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid joint inference for a simplex optimizer and its functional at one fixed population objective through polyhedral-cone projection.
Theorems 1--2 and Theorem A give probability-guaranteed prediction intervals for a future synthetic-control counterfactual after propagating estimated-weight and post-regime errors.

Definition 1 restricts bands to those induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area; Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, with low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation supplied specifically for weighted area.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 give Bayes--minimax duality for confidence sets under expected additive measure, and Theorem 2 solves a bounded one-dimensional shift family.
Theorem 2 proves convergence of a Monte Carlo approximation to a finite-prior minimax expected-measure confidence procedure.
Theorem 3.1 and its corollaries derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for scalar linear functionals over convex Gaussian regression classes.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 characterize ordinary-bootstrap failure and validate derivative-aware resampling for a fixed directionally differentiable functional.
Propositions 3.1--3.6 provide active-set degrees of freedom and information criteria for selecting synthetic-control penalties or predictor-weighting matrices.

body.tldr: Predictor weighting changes both the donor face and the future counterfactual performance of a synthetic control. This paper identifies the entire population prediction-MSE graph from the stated block-stable fixed-rank panel, constructs a uniformly valid root-\(n\) same-panel band over the predictor simplex, and computes the exact compact-local iid-Gaussian minimax expected maximum width through finite KKT-cell, conic-distance, and primal--dual linear programs with certified vanishing error. Exact attainment is local to the specified Gaussian neighborhoods; the global projection band is validity-only. Every procedure uniformly honest over the full panel class nevertheless obeys the computed local lower bound because that honesty requirement contains the Gaussian paths.

project_justification.gap: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection and PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom make predictor selection operational but do not attach an honest population-risk certificate to every candidate weighting. CanenSong2026SimplexWeight treats one fixed simplex objective. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and develops low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation for weighted area; other minimum-size confidence-set results treat scalar linear targets or additive set-measure losses. None addresses an unrestricted externally randomized max-curve-diameter decision for a piecewise-affine risk curve whose KKT face moves with the local query.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the observable graph \(G_P\) together with the exact compact-local price, measured by worst-case expected maximum interval width, of covering that graph when predictor and moment perturbations move donor faces on the same root-\(n\) scale.
project_justification.fill: The paper combines row-span completion, a joint block-mean and covariance expansion, exact shifted-QP inversion, critical-cone curve geometry, and certified finite primal and dual decision programs. Bidirectional vanishing-deficiency transfer between the observed iid-Gaussian panel and its Gaussian shift proves the matching compact-local lower bound and attainment. The broader mixing-class result is uniform validity of the global projection band; only the lower bound, not Gaussian-local attainment, transfers to every honesty class containing the Gaussian paths.

body.related_work: CanenSong2026SimplexWeight, Theorem 3.1, is a high-level fixed-objective result under uniform joint asymptotic normality, nondegeneracy, and variance consistency. Its explicit synthetic-control example instead uses repeated cross-sections with iid individuals within dates and positive group shares; the fixed-cross-section long panel here may instantiate the abstract theorem separately at a fixed predictor weight, but it is not that published example. VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection studies an aggregate fixed-dimensional long panel with time-varying linear factors, oracle separation and injectivity, and an \(\ell_1\)-penalized bilevel predictor-selection objective, rather than this fixed-ridge block-stable class. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021PredictionIntervals allows a fixed-unit stationary weakly dependent time series but targets future-counterfactual and treatment-effect prediction intervals, not simultaneous inference for a population-MSE graph. FangSantos2019Directional explains the failure of ordinary bootstrap reasoning at nonsmooth maps. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence, SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions, and ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference provide related decision-theoretic architectures, but not the unrestricted externally randomized maximum-curve-width problem for a moving-KKT risk graph. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands studies bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and develops its main approximation for weighted-area loss; no strict numerical separation from that work is asserted here. The present results are derived for the displayed panel class itself, not by identifying it with any of these published classes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The KKT atlas, critical-cone risk map, certified LP/SOCP approximation, bidirectional Gaussian-panel deficiency transfer, and compact-local minimax theorem are established in the core. The remaining limitation is one of scope rather than an open proof step: the projection band over the stationary mixing class is a validity construction only, whereas exact decision optimality and attainment are proved on compact iid-Gaussian local experiments. Uniform honesty over the larger class implies the same local lower bound, but the locally attaining Gaussian procedures have not been shown uniformly valid or attaining over that larger class. No compulsory positive cost from a face change and no strict separation from existing generic band theory is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The global mixing-class band and the locally optimal Gaussian-neighborhood bands are different procedures. The global projection band \(C_n\) is proved uniformly valid but is not claimed to be globally minimax. Exact optimality and attainment concern fixed-dimensional, compact iid-Gaussian local neighborhoods with known spectrally separated rank, fixed positive ridge, stable block means, and a stable donor post regime. The converse is broader: any band sequence uniformly honest over the full panel class is honest on the contained Gaussian paths and must have compact-local scaled expected maximum width at least \(L_\alpha\). The reverse implication is not proved, so Gaussian-local attainment gives no global-class attainment claim. Unknown rank, growing dimensions, singleton-date predictors, post-factor drift, shrinking ridge, direct guarantees for the different objectives in Synth or SparseSC, and optimal inference for a corrected causal treatment effect remain outside scope.
